exercises.name: Aerobics

source_english.description: Aerobics is a rhythmic sequence of low- to moderate-impact steps and arm patterns performed continuously for the selected duration.
instructions: Stand tall with relaxed shoulders and begin with easy marching.
Add coordinated arm and leg patterns while keeping a comfortable rhythm.
Progress the pace or pattern without losing stable foot placement.
Continue for the planned duration, then gradually slow down.
source_english.safety_note: Use a clear, non-slip floor and lower the pace before footwork becomes unstable.

exercises.name: Ball Slams

source_english.description: Ball Slams raise a medicine ball overhead and drive it into the floor using the hips, trunk, and arms together.
instructions: Stand with feet about shoulder-width apart and hold the medicine ball overhead with both hands.
Brace your trunk and bend the hips and knees slightly.
Drive the ball forcefully into the floor in front of you.
Retrieve it with a squat or hinge and reset before the next repetition.
form_cues: Keep the ball in front of you.
Use the hips and trunk together.
common_mistakes: Catching a rebound with locked knees.
source_english.safety_note: Use a slam-rated medicine ball and keep the rebound area clear.

exercises.name: Battle Ropes

source_english.description: Battle Ropes create alternating waves from a stable athletic stance, with the rope motion traveling toward its anchor.
instructions: Stand with a soft bend in the knees and hold one rope end in each hand.
Brace your trunk and create alternating waves by lifting and lowering the hands.
Keep the waves traveling toward the anchor rather than swinging the torso.
Work for the planned interval, then lower the ropes under control.
form_cues: Match the wave to your breathing.
common_mistakes: Leaning back against the rope tension.
source_english.safety_note: Secure the rope anchor and keep both feet planted during waves.

exercises.name: Boxing

source_english.description: Boxing alternates straight punches and hooks with light footwork, returning each hand to guard between strikes.
instructions: Stand in a balanced stance with hands near the face.
Throw controlled straight punches and hooks while rotating through the hips.
Return each hand to guard before the opposite punch.
Continue for the planned interval and slow the footwork before stopping.
source_english.safety_note: Use clear space and stop before punches lose wrist and shoulder alignment.

exercises.name: Burpee Over the Bar

source_english.description: Burpee Over the Bar combines a squat-to-plank transition with a lateral jump over the bar.
instructions: Stand tall, squat, and place the hands on the floor.
Step or jump both feet back into a plank, then return them under the hips.
Stand and jump sideways over the bar, landing on the opposite side.
Turn or reset under control before the next repetition.
source_english.safety_note: Use a step-back or step-over version if the plank or landing cannot stay controlled.

exercises.name: Clean

source_english.description: Clean begins with the barbell near the legs, uses a powerful extension, and receives the load at the shoulders with soft knees.
instructions: Start with the barbell in front of the legs and brace the trunk.
Drive through the floor or hips to bring the load close to the body.
Receive it at the shoulders with soft knees and elbows under the load.
Lower it under control and reset before the next repetition.
source_english.safety_note: Use a clear area and a load that can be safely caught at the shoulders.

source_english.description: Clean and Jerk combines a barbell clean to the shoulders with a dip-and-drive overhead jerk.
instructions: Start with the barbell from the floor and keep the back neutral.
Extend the hips and knees to pull the load into the rack position.
Dip slightly and drive overhead into a stable split or power stance.
Lower the load safely and reset each repetition.
source_english.safety_note: Use a light practice load until the rack and overhead receiving positions are stable.

exercises.name: Clean Pull

source_english.description: Clean Pull starts from the floor and uses leg and hip extension to bring the bar upward without receiving it in a front-rack catch.
instructions: Stand with the bar over midfoot, hinge down, and grip it just outside the legs with the shins close to the bar.
Brace, push through the floor, and extend the hips and knees together.
Pull the bar upward with elbows high while keeping it close to the body.
Lower under control without turning the pull into a catch.
form_cues: Do not yank with the arms first.
source_english.safety_note: Use a clear lifting lane and keep the bar close to the body.

exercises.name: Deadlift High Pull

source_english.description: Deadlift High Pull hinges to the barbell, drives the floor away, and finishes with the hips tall before reversing the hinge.
instructions: Stand over the barbell and hinge to grip it with a neutral spine.
Drive through the floor and extend the hips and knees to stand tall.
After hip extension, pull the bar toward the upper chest with elbows high.
Lower the bar under control and reset.
form_cues: Keep the shoulders over the bar or weights.
Finish with glutes, not lumbar extension.
source_english.safety_note: Use a load that allows a neutral spine from setup through lockout.

source_english.description: Dumbbell Snatch accelerates dumbbells from the floor or hang into a stable overhead position in one continuous lift.
instructions: Start with the dumbbells close to the body and keep the spine neutral.
Drive through the legs and hips, keeping the load close as it rises.
Pull under or guide the weight to a stable overhead position with the arm locked out.
Lower safely and reset for the next repetition.
source_english.safety_note: Use a light load and clear overhead space until the catch is stable.

source_english.description: Front Lever Hold suspends the body in a straight horizontal line from the bar without swinging.
instructions: Hang from a secure bar with an overhand grip.
Brace the core and pull the shoulders down as the legs extend forward.
Hold the body in a straight horizontal line for the planned duration.
Lower with control and release the bar safely.
source_english.safety_note: Use a tucked progression and a secure bar before attempting a full lever.

exercises.name: Front Lever Raise

source_english.description: Front Lever Raise lifts the legs and hips toward a horizontal lever line, then lowers under control.
instructions: Hang from a secure bar and begin with the body under control.
Brace the core and raise the legs and hips toward a horizontal front-lever line.
Pause briefly at the highest controlled position.
Lower slowly to the starting hang and repeat.
common_mistakes: Bending the knees to hide lost control.
source_english.safety_note: Stop the raise before swinging or shoulder control is lost.

exercises.name: Handstand Hold

source_english.description: Handstand Hold balances the body upside down on straight arms with the ribs and pelvis aligned.
instructions: Place your hands on a clear surface about shoulder-width apart.

Hold the position with steady breathing and active shoulders.
Lower one foot at a time with control.

exercises.name: Hang Clean

source_english.description: Hang Clean begins with the barbell near the legs, uses a powerful extension, and receives the load at the shoulders with soft knees.
instructions: Stand with the barbell at thigh height and hands just outside the legs.
Hinge slightly, then drive the hips and knees to accelerate the bar close to the body.
Pull under and receive the bar on the front shoulders with soft knees.
Lower the bar to the hang and reset.
source_english.safety_note: Use a clear area and a load that can be safely caught at the shoulders.

exercises.name: Hang Snatch

source_english.description: Hang Snatch accelerates barbell from the floor or hang into a stable overhead position in one continuous lift.
instructions: Start with the barbell close to the body and keep the spine neutral.
Drive through the legs and hips, keeping the load close as it rises.
Pull under or guide the weight to a stable overhead position with the arm locked out.
Lower safely and reset for the next repetition.
source_english.safety_note: Use a light load and clear overhead space until the catch is stable.

source_english.description: Hiking is sustained walking over changing terrain, with pace and footing adjusted to the route.
instructions: Choose a safe route and begin at an easy walking pace.
Maintain a steady stride over the terrain while looking ahead.
Adjust pace and footing for climbs, descents, and uneven ground.
Continue for the planned distance or duration, then cool down with easy walking.
common_mistakes: Starting without water or suitable footing.
source_english.safety_note: Check the route, weather, footwear, and hydration before a long outing.

exercises.name: Jump Rope

source_english.description: Turn the rope with the hands and make light repeated jumps as it passes beneath the feet.
instructions: Hold the handles of the jump rope with your hands, palms facing inward.
Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and knees slightly bent.
Swing the rope over your head and jump over it as it comes towards your feet.
Land softly on the balls of your feet and repeat the jump as the rope comes around again.
Continue jumping for the desired duration or number of repetitions.
source_english.safety_note: Choose a pace and surface that allow controlled breathing and stable landings.

exercises.name: Jump Shrug

source_english.description: A barbell jump shrug combines explosive hip and knee extension with a powerful shoulder shrug before a soft landing.
instructions: Stand with the barbell at the thighs, feet about hip-width apart, and hands just outside the legs.
Dip slightly at the knees and hips while keeping the back neutral.
Drive through the floor, extend the hips and knees, and shrug the shoulders as the bar rises.
Land softly with bent knees and lower the bar under control.
form_cues: Finish tall through the hips before the shrug.
Land quietly with the knees aligned.
common_mistakes: Pulling with the arms before extending the hips.
Jumping forward or letting the bar drift away.
source_english.safety_note: Use a light load and clear the landing area before performing the jump.

exercises.name: Kettlebell Clean

source_english.description: A kettlebell clean uses a hip-driven close path to bring the bell from between the legs into the rack position.
instructions: Stand with the kettlebell between your feet and hinge at the hips with a neutral back.
Hike the bell back, then drive the hips forward to guide it upward close to the body.
Rotate the hand around the handle and receive the bell softly against the forearm in the rack position.
Lower it back between the legs with control and repeat on the same or opposite side.
form_cues: Use the hips rather than an arm curl.
Keep the bell close to the body.
Relax the grip as the bell rotates.
common_mistakes: Letting the bell swing far forward.
Catching it with a bent wrist.
Squatting under the bell instead of hinging.
source_english.safety_note: Start with a light kettlebell and keep the forearm and wrist aligned in the rack.

source_english.description: From a wide stance, drive the hips and pull the kettlebell upward with the elbows high and wide.
instructions: Stand with your feet wider than shoulder-width apart, toes pointing outwards.
Hold a kettlebell with both hands in front of your body, arms extended downwards.
Bend your knees and lower your hips into a squat position, keeping your back straight.
Drive through your heels and explosively extend your hips and knees, pulling the kettlebell up towards your chin.
As you pull the kettlebell up, keep your elbows high and wide, and squeeze your shoulder blades together.
Lower the kettlebell back down to the starting position and repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
form_cues: Keep the kettlebell close and let the elbows rise above the handle.
source_english.safety_note: Use a comfortable range and stop if control or alignment deteriorates.

source_english.description: Swing one kettlebell from between the legs to an overhead lockout in one fluid pull.
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a kettlebell in one hand between your legs.
Bend your knees slightly and hinge at the hips, lowering the kettlebell towards the ground.
Explosively extend your hips and knees, using the momentum to swing the kettlebell up towards your shoulder.
As the kettlebell reaches shoulder height, rotate your hand and punch it straight up overhead, fully extending your arm.
Lower the kettlebell back down between your legs and repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
form_cues: Keep the kettlebell close as the hips drive it to a stable overhead lockout.
source_english.safety_note: Use a comfortable range and stop if control or alignment deteriorates.

exercises.name: Kettlebell Swing

source_english.description: Hinge the hips to load the kettlebell behind you, then drive forward so it floats to shoulder height.
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, toes pointed slightly outward.
Hold the kettlebell with both hands in front of your body, arms extended.
Bend your knees slightly and hinge at the hips, pushing your butt back.
Swing the kettlebell back between your legs, keeping your arms straight and maintaining a flat back.
Drive your hips forward and swing the kettlebell up to shoulder height, using the momentum generated by your hips.
Allow the kettlebell to swing back down between your legs and repeat the movement for the desired number of repetitions.
form_cues: Let the hips drive the kettlebell; do not lift it with the arms.
source_english.safety_note: Use a comfortable range and stop if control or alignment deteriorates.

instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, toes pointed slightly outward.
Hold the kettlebell with both hands in front of your body, arms extended.
Bend your knees slightly and hinge at the hips, pushing your butt back.
Swing the kettlebell back between your legs, keeping your arms straight and maintaining a flat back.
Drive your hips forward and swing the kettlebell up to shoulder height, using the momentum generated by your hips.
Allow the kettlebell to swing back down between your legs and repeat the movement for the desired number of repetitions.
form_cues: Let the hips drive the kettlebell; do not lift it with the arms.

exercises.name: Kettlebell Turkish Get Up

source_english.description: A Turkish get-up moves from the floor to standing and back while one kettlebell remains locked overhead.
instructions: Lie on your back with the kettlebell locked out over one shoulder and the same-side knee bent.
Press through the foot to lift the hips, then sweep the opposite leg under into a supported half-kneel.
Rotate upright, stand while keeping the kettlebell overhead, and stabilize.
Reverse the sequence step by step to return to the floor, then switch sides.
form_cues: Keep the kettlebell vertically above the shoulder through each floor-to-stand transition.
source_english.safety_note: Use a comfortable range and stop if control or alignment deteriorates.

exercises.name: Landmine Squat and Press

source_english.description: A landmine squat and press combines a squat with a forward-and-up press of the anchored barbell.
instructions: Stand facing the free end of the landmine bar and hold it at the chest with both hands.
Squat by bending the knees and hips while keeping the chest lifted.
Drive through the feet to stand and press the bar forward and upward.
Lower the bar to the chest as you prepare for the next controlled squat.
form_cues: Keep the bar close to the sternum.
Track the knees over the toes.
Finish the press without leaning back.
common_mistakes: Dropping the chest in the squat.
Arching the back under the bar.
source_english.safety_note: Use a clear forward path and a load that does not pull you off balance.

exercises.name: Muscle Up

source_english.description: Pull from a hang and transition the torso over the bar before pressing to support.
instructions: Start by hanging from a pull-up bar with your palms facing away from you and your arms fully extended.
Engage your core and pull your body up towards the bar, leading with your chest.
As you reach the top of the movement, transition your grip so that your palms are facing towards you.
Continue pulling yourself up until your chest is above the bar and your arms are fully flexed.
Reverse the movement by slowly lowering yourself back down to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
form_cues: Keep the kip controlled as the chest rises over the bar before the press.
source_english.safety_note: Use a comfortable range and stop if control or alignment deteriorates.

source_english.description: Pull from a hang and transition the torso over the bar before pressing to support.
instructions: Start by hanging from a pull-up bar with your palms facing away from you and your arms fully extended.
Engage your core and pull your body up towards the bar, leading with your chest.
As you reach the top of the movement, transition your grip so that your palms are facing towards you.
Continue pulling yourself up until your chest is above the bar and your arms are fully flexed.
Reverse the movement by slowly lowering yourself back down to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
form_cues: Keep the kip controlled as the chest rises over the bar before the press.
source_english.safety_note: Use a comfortable range and stop if control or alignment deteriorates.

exercises.name: Overhead Squat

source_english.description: Hold the barbell overhead while squatting through the hips and knees with the arms locked.
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and toes slightly turned out.
Hold the barbell with a wide grip, positioning it overhead with your arms fully extended.
Engage your core and lower your body down into a squat position, keeping your chest up and knees tracking over your toes.
Pause for a moment at the bottom, then push through your heels to return to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
form_cues: Track the knees with the toes.
Keep the chest and trunk controlled.
source_english.safety_note: Use a depth and load that allow a stable knee and hip path.

form_cues: Keep the joints aligned while following the concrete movement arc.
source_english.safety_note: Use a comfortable range and stop if control or alignment deteriorates.

Press the bar upward while actively moving the body underneath it.
Finish with the bar overhead and elbows locked, then return it to the start.
common_mistakes: Receiving with bent or uneven arms.
source_english.safety_note: Use an empty bar or light load and a rack with safety supports.

exercises.name: Running

source_english.description: Running uses a repeating stride with relaxed posture, soft foot contact, and a steady forward or in-place rhythm.
instructions: Start by standing upright with your feet hip-width apart.
Engage your core and keep your upper body relaxed.
Begin jogging in place, lifting your knees up towards your chest and landing softly on the balls of your feet.
Maintain a steady pace and continue jogging for the desired duration or distance.
Remember to breathe deeply and maintain good posture throughout the exercise.
source_english.safety_note: Choose a pace and surface that allow controlled breathing and stable landings.

exercises.name: Skating

source_english.description: Skating uses repeated side-to-side bounds with one-foot landings and the free leg sweeping behind the body.
instructions: Stand with feet hip-width apart and bend the knees slightly.
Bound to the right and land softly on the right foot.
Swing the left leg behind the right and tap the floor, then bound to the left.
Alternate sides while keeping the landings quiet and controlled.
form_cues: Keep the chest angled slightly forward.
Push sideways through the whole foot.
source_english.safety_note: Use a non-slip surface and reduce the distance if single-leg landings become unstable.

exercises.name: Skiing

source_english.description: Skiing is a cardio movement that alternates quick diagonal steps and arm swings as if pushing across snow.
instructions: Stand in an athletic stance with knees softly bent and arms ready in front.
Step diagonally to the right while driving the left arm forward.
Step diagonally to the left while driving the right arm forward.
Continue alternating at a steady rhythm with the torso slightly inclined.
common_mistakes: Leaning so far forward that balance is lost.
source_english.safety_note: Use a clear, level surface and keep the pace low enough to place each foot deliberately.

exercises.name: Sled Pull

source_english.description: A sled pull drags a weighted sled toward you using a rope or strap while you walk backward with short steps.
instructions: Attach the rope or strap securely and face the sled with the line held at waist height.
Brace the trunk, sit the hips slightly back, and take a short backward step.
Continue walking backward while keeping steady tension on the line.
Stop when the sled reaches the planned distance and lower the rope before turning.
common_mistakes: Rounding the back to start the sled.
source_english.safety_note: Check the attachment and keep the path clear of obstacles before pulling.

exercises.name: Snatch

source_english.description: A barbell snatch pulls the bar from the floor and catches it overhead in a deep receiving squat before standing tall.
instructions: Set the bar over the mid-foot with a wide overhand grip and a flat back.
Lift close to the legs, then extend the hips and knees powerfully.
Pull under the bar and catch it overhead with locked elbows in a deep squat.
Stand by driving through the feet, then lower the bar to the floor under control.
form_cues: Finish the extension before pulling under.
Stack the bar over the shoulders.
source_english.safety_note: Use a light load, clear overhead space, and stop if the catch is uneven.

exercises.name: Snowboarding

source_english.description: Snowboarding is a balance and cardio activity performed in a sideways stance while the legs flex and extend to steer.
instructions: Stand sideways on a board with the feet secured and knees softly bent.
Shift pressure between the heels and toes to control the board edge.
Keep the hips centered over the board while gliding and steering.
Slow down by increasing edge pressure before stopping.
form_cues: Look in the direction of travel.
Center the hips over the board.
common_mistakes: Leaning the shoulders far outside the board.
source_english.safety_note: Use appropriate protective gear and a beginner-appropriate slope or training surface.

exercises.name: Split Jerk

source_english.description: A barbell split jerk drives the bar overhead with a leg dip and catches it in a split stance before recovering.
instructions: Hold the barbell at the shoulders with elbows slightly forward and feet hip-width apart.
Dip straight down, then drive forcefully through the legs to propel the bar upward.
Split one foot forward and the other back as you press under the bar with locked elbows.
Bring the front foot back and rear foot forward to recover, then lower the bar.
form_cues: Lock the bar over the shoulders.
common_mistakes: Recovering with the wrong foot first.
source_english.safety_note: Use a rack, clear overhead space, and a light load while learning the split.

exercises.name: Sprints

source_english.description: Sprints are short, fast running efforts separated by walking or standing recovery.
instructions: Choose a measured straight path and begin with an easy warm-up pace.
Accelerate with a forward lean, driving the knees and arms in opposition.
Run hard for the planned distance or time while keeping the stride controlled.
Decelerate gradually, recover, and repeat only after breathing settles.
form_cues: Keep the foot strike under the hips.
Drive the arms straight ahead and back.
common_mistakes: Starting at maximum speed without a warm-up.
source_english.safety_note: Use a clear, level surface and stop if stride mechanics or balance deteriorate.

source_english.description: Stretching uses slow, deliberate positions to move a chosen muscle group through a comfortable range without bouncing.
instructions: Choose one target area and set a relaxed posture that does not twist the joints.
Move slowly into a mild stretch while breathing evenly.
Hold the position without bouncing or forcing the end range.
Return to neutral gradually before changing sides or positions.
common_mistakes: Forcing pain instead of mild tension.
source_english.safety_note: Stretch only within a comfortable range and stop if sharp pain, numbness, or dizziness occurs.

exercises.name: Suitcase Carry (Dumbbell)

source_english.description: A dumbbell suitcase carry walks while one heavy dumbbell hangs at one side, challenging the trunk to resist leaning.
instructions: Stand tall with one dumbbell at your side and the other arm relaxed.
Brace the abdomen and keep the shoulders and hips level.
Walk forward with short, controlled steps while keeping the dumbbell from touching the thigh.
Stop at the planned distance, set the weight down safely, and switch sides.
common_mistakes: Leaning toward or away from the dumbbell.
Turning before the weight is controlled.
source_english.safety_note: Use a clear walking lane and a weight you can set down without dropping.

exercises.name: Swimming

source_english.description: Swimming is a prone alternating arm-and-leg pattern that mimics a gentle swim stroke for continuous cardio.
instructions: Lie face down with arms extended overhead and legs straight.
Lift the right arm with the left leg while the opposite pair stays long.
Switch sides in a steady alternating rhythm without lifting the ribs high.
Continue for the planned interval, then lower the limbs.
source_english.safety_note: Use a small range and stop if the lower back cannot stay relaxed.

exercises.name: Thruster (Barbell)

source_english.description: Thruster (Barbell) combines a front-rack barbell squat with an immediate overhead press.
instructions: Stand with feet shoulder-width apart and hold the barbell in the front-rack position.
Squat by bending the hips and knees while keeping the chest lifted.
Drive through the feet to stand and use the same momentum to press the load overhead.
Lower the load to the shoulders, then descend into the next squat.
form_cues: Finish the leg drive before pressing.
common_mistakes: Dropping the load to the shoulders.
source_english.safety_note: Use a load you can lower safely to the shoulders after every press.

instructions: Stand with feet shoulder-width apart and hold one kettlebell at the chest.
Squat by bending the hips and knees while keeping the chest lifted.
Drive through the feet to stand and use the same momentum to press the load overhead.
Lower the load to the shoulders, then descend into the next squat.
form_cues: Finish the leg drive before pressing.
common_mistakes: Dropping the load to the shoulders.
source_english.safety_note: Use a load you can lower safely to the shoulders after every press.

exercises.name: Walking

source_english.description: Walking is continuous upright locomotion at a controlled pace, with each step rolling from heel to toe.
instructions: Stand tall on a clear walking surface with arms relaxed.
Step forward with one foot and place the heel under the body.
Roll through the foot and push off the toes as the opposite leg swings forward.
Continue at the programmed pace and slow to an easy walk before stopping.
source_english.safety_note: Use a clear route and appropriate footwear for the walking duration.

exercises.name: Wall Ball

source_english.description: Wall Ball squats with a medicine ball at the chest and throws it vertically to a wall target.
instructions: Stand facing a wall with feet shoulder-width apart and hold the medicine ball at the chest.
Squat until the thighs approach parallel while keeping heels down.
Drive through the legs and release the ball upward toward the wall target.
Catch it at chest height, absorb the catch, and descend into the next squat.
form_cues: Keep the ball close before the throw.
common_mistakes: Standing too close to the wall.
source_english.safety_note: Use a wall and ball rated for impacts and keep the catch zone clear.

instructions: Stand facing a wall with feet shoulder-width apart and hold the medicine ball at the chest.
Squat until the thighs approach parallel while keeping heels down.
Drive through the legs and release the ball upward toward the wall target.
Catch it at chest height, absorb the catch, and descend into the next squat.
form_cues: Keep the ball close before the throw.
common_mistakes: Standing too close to the wall.
source_english.safety_note: Use a wall and ball rated for impacts and keep the catch zone clear.

source_english.description: Warm Up raises temperature and joint readiness through easy whole-body movements before harder work.
instructions: Begin with easy marching and arm swings for several minutes.

Gradually increase the range and pace without fatigue.
Finish with relaxed movement before starting the main session.
source_english.safety_note: Keep the warm-up below fatigue and use movements that leave joints comfortable.

source_english.description: Downward Dog lifts the hips up and back from the hands, lengthening the spine while the knees may stay softly bent.
instructions: Start on hands and knees with hands under the shoulders.
Press the floor away and lift the hips up and back.
Keep the spine long and bend the knees as needed.
Hold steady breaths, then return to the hands-and-knees position.
source_english.safety_note: Keep the wrist load within a comfortable range and do not force the heels down.

source_english.description: Bear Crawl keeps the knees hovering while opposite hands and feet advance in short, controlled steps.
instructions: Start on hands and feet with knees hovering just above the floor.
Move the opposite hand and foot forward together.
Keep the hips low and continue alternating without rotating the trunk.
Reverse or continue for the planned distance or time.
source_english.safety_note: Clear the floor and stop before wrist or shoulder support breaks down.

source_english.description: Jump the feet apart as the arms rise overhead, then return both to the starting position.
instructions: Stand with your feet together and your arms by your sides.
Jump up, spreading your feet apart and raising your arms above your head.
As you land, quickly jump back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
source_english.safety_note: Choose a pace and surface that allow controlled breathing and stable landings.

source_english.description: High Knees alternates knee drives toward hip height with the torso upright and each foot landing softly.
instructions: Stand tall with arms relaxed and brace the abdomen.
Drive the right knee toward hip height while the left foot supports the body.
Switch legs with a small hop for skips or a quick step for high knees.
Continue alternating for the programmed repetitions.
source_english.safety_note: Use a clear, non-slip surface and lower the cadence before knee or ankle control fades.

source_english.description: From a high plank, alternate driving the knees toward the chest while the shoulders stay over the hands.
instructions: Start in a high plank position with your hands directly under your shoulders and your body in a straight line.
Engage your core and bring your right knee towards your chest, then quickly switch and bring your left knee towards your chest.
Continue alternating legs in a running motion, keeping your hips low and your core engaged.
Maintain a steady pace and breathe evenly throughout the exercise.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
form_cues: Keep shoulders over hands while each knee drives toward the chest.
source_english.safety_note: Use a comfortable range and stop if control or alignment deteriorates.
